rationale: Title of Kephalaion 46. Standard Manichaean cosmological enumeration distributing the entire archontic host into four kinds: (1) powers in the ten firmaments above the wheel, (2) the eight earths below joined to four places of darkness, (3) preparations and strongholds surrounding the worlds, (4) the sphere of stars. Functions as the principal organizing schema for cosmic powers in Manichaean cosmography.

Cosmological term: the ten firmaments above the wheel of stars (distinct from the seven firmaments below, e.g. ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲁϣⲭ ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ in glossary). The total cosmic firmament-count of seventeen or eighteen is canonical Manichaean.
Manichaean technical term for the eight infernal earths of the lower cosmos, paired/joined with the four places of darkness. Forms the lower cosmographic register of the Four Great Works.

Compound: ⲱⲁⲣⲡ 'first' (Lyc. for ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄, in glossary) + Greek ἀρχιτέκτων. Title of the Great Builder (Living Spirit) as the foremost architect responsible for constructing the New Aeon at the eschaton. Parallels ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲓⲧⲉⲕⲧⲱⲛ in the accumulated vocabulary.

Agent-noun ⲣⲉϥ- + ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('release forth,' in glossary). The cosmic agents commissioned to release/dissolve the world at the end. Parallels other ⲣⲉϥ-/ⲣⲉϩ- agentives in the glossary (ⲡⲣⲉϩⲃⲱⲗ 'the Releaser,' ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeemer,' etc.).

ⲧⲁⲓⲱⲛ (Greek αἰών) + ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ ('new,' Lyc. variant of ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ; cf. ⲣⲙⲉⲉ in glossary). Manichaean eschatological term for the renewed cosmic order constructed by the Great Builder and his angels after the present world's release.

Greek τροχός 'wheel' + ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲟⲩ 'of stars.' Standard Manichaean cosmological term for the visible celestial sphere (zodiac/sphere of fixed stars), here distinguished from ⲧⲥⲫⲁⲓⲣⲁ ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲟⲩ 'the sphere of stars' (line 32) — the wheel being the upper-side rotating axis, the sphere being the totality.

Greek σφαῖρα 'sphere' + Coptic 'of stars.' The fourth great work: the cosmic sphere of stars characterized as lying 'in great shame, being heavy.' The shamed/heavy character reflects Manichaean negative valuation of the visible heavens as bondage of light-particles.

proposed_english: the four places of the Darkness
rationale: Compound cosmographic term: the four cosmic loci of the Darkness, joined to the four lower of the eight earths. Forms the dark-cosmographic counterpart to the four upper places.

Plural of ⲥⲃⲧⲉ/ⲥⲟⲃⲧⲉ 'prepare; preparation, equipment, fortification.' In the third kind the 'preparations' are paired with 'strongholds' (ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲟⲣⲉ) as the cosmic defensive-architectural apparatus surrounding the worlds. Could also be rendered 'fortifications' if construed as architectural rather than the procedural sense.

Already in glossary as 'kind/category'; this page confirms it as the principal enumerative cosmological term for the four cosmic divisions. Each ⲧⲁⲓⲉ is a register of cosmic powers/places. Direct correspondential register: each ⲧⲁⲓⲉ IS a cosmic division of the archontic host.
